subject: Literacy
title: Sharing a picture book
subtopics: Holding a book and turning pages
objectives: Children will hold a book the right way up and turn pages.
Children will point to and name pictures.
content: Holding a book the right way up, turning pages, pointing to and naming pictures, and sharing a favourite book.
teachingActivities: Hold the book so every child can see; run your finger under the pictures; name each picture and wait for the child to say it; let children turn pages with you.
learnerActivities: Hold a book the right way up, turn pages one at a time, point to and name pictures.
resources: Sturdy board books with large pictures
assessment: Observe whether each child holds a book correctly, turns pages and names three pictures.
expectedOutcomes: Turns pages one at a time with support.
Names three pictures in a book.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: looking at pictures

lessons.title: This is a book
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Holding a book and turning pages
objectives: Children will hold a book the right way up and say or show that it is a book.
successCriteria: Holds a book the right way up
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join in rhymes, name animals and greet others, and many point to pictures.
lessons.starter: Hold up a book and say "This is a book. Look at the front." Turn it upside down and say "Oops!" Turn it the right way and say "Now we can see."
teacherActivities: Show the front, the back and the spine. Say "This is the front."
Give each child a book and say "Hold it the right way up."
Show how to turn a page gently and say "Turn the page".
Walk round and say each child’s name and "Well done holding your book".
learnerActivities: Children look and point to the front.
Child holds the book the right way up with support.
Children copy turning a page.
Child smiles and shows their book.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the front, the back and the spine. Say "This is the front." Children: Children look and point to the front.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a book and say "Hold it the right way up." Children: Child holds the book the right way up with support.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to turn a page gently and say "Turn the page". Children: Children copy turning a page.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk round and say each child’s name and "Well done holding your book". Children: Child smiles and shows their book.

practical.title: Book time
steps: Give each child a board book and sit comfortably.
Children hold the book and turn pages.
Say "page" each time a page is turned.
practical.safety: Use sturdy board books with rounded corners. Keep books off the floor and do not allow chewing.

differentiation.support: Hold the book together and turn each page with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find the front of the book and show a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Holds a book the right way up with support
lessons.conclusion: Close the books and put them back in the basket together.
lessons.homeConnection: Share a book at home every day and let your child turn the pages.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hold a book the right way up and say or show that it is a book" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Open the book, turn the page. Look and see, look and see.

lessons.title: Turning the pages
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Holding a book and turning pages
objectives: Children will turn the pages of a book one at a time.
successCriteria: Turns one page at a time with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join in rhymes, name animals and greet others, and many point to pictures.
lessons.starter: Open the book slowly and say "Open, open, what can we see?" Turn a page and say "Another page."
teacherActivities: Show a page and say "Turn the page" while turning it.
Let each child come forward to turn a page of the big book.
Ask "What is on this page?" and wait.
Let the children turn the pages of their own books.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say "page".
Child turns the page with support.
Child points to or names the picture.
Child turns pages one at a time.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a page and say "Turn the page" while turning it. Children: Children watch and say "page".
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child come forward to turn a page of the big book. Children: Child turns the page with support.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What is on this page?" and wait. Children: Child points to or names the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Let the children turn the pages of their own books. Children: Child turns pages one at a time.

practical.title: Book corner
steps: Set up cushions and board books.
Each child chooses a book and turns pages.
Name a picture on each page with a friend.
practical.safety: Keep the book corner uncluttered. Show children to sit with space between them and to handle books gently.

differentiation.support: Use a book with thick pages and turn the pages together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to turn the pages for a friend and name the pictures.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Turns pages one at a time with support
lessons.conclusion: Close the book and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child turn the pages while you point to the pictures.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "turn the pages of a book one at a time" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Pointing to pictures
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will point to and name pictures in a book.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join in rhymes, name animals and greet others, and many point to pictures.
resources: A picture book with clear pictures of a dog, a ball, a cup and a baby
lessons.starter: Open the book and say "Where is the dog? Point to the dog." Point yourself first.
teacherActivities: Point to each picture and say its name clearly.
Say a name and ask "Where is the ball?"
Point to a picture and ask "What is this?" and wait.
Let each child point to a picture and ask "What is this?"
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children point to the ball.
Child names the picture or says a sound.
Child points and the group names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Point to each picture and say its name clearly. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a name and ask "Where is the ball?" Children: Children point to the ball.
Step 3. Teacher: Point to a picture and ask "What is this?" and wait. Children: Child names the picture or says a sound.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child point to a picture and ask "What is this?" Children: Child points and the group names it.

practical.title: I spy a picture
steps: Open a book to a page with four pictures.
Children point to the dog. Repeat for the other pictures.
practical.safety: Keep the book low so children can see. Remind children to touch pictures gently and not tear pages.

differentiation.support: Point together and say the name before the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name three pictures in a row.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Close the book and say "Goodbye, dog, ball, cup, baby."
lessons.homeConnection: Point to pictures in a book at home and ask "Where is the ball?"
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to and name pictures in a book" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My favourite book
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will choose a favourite book and share it with a friend.
successCriteria: Shows or tells a friend about a picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join in rhymes, name animals and greet others, and many point to pictures.
lessons.starter: Put four books on the mat and say "Which book do you like? Choose one."
teacherActivities: Show each book front cover and say its name or topic.
Let each child pick a book and sit with a friend.
Ask each pair to look at the book together.
Walk round and ask "What do you like?"
learnerActivities: Children look and point to the one they like.
Child chooses and sits with a friend.
Children turn pages and point to pictures.
Child shows a picture or says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each book front cover and say its name or topic. Children: Children look and point to the one they like.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child pick a book and sit with a friend. Children: Child chooses and sits with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask each pair to look at the book together. Children: Children turn pages and point to pictures.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk round and ask "What do you like?" Children: Child shows a picture or says a word.

practical.title: Share with a friend
steps: Children take turns to turn pages and point.
practical.safety: Check that books have no loose parts. Sit friends with space so they do not squash the book.

differentiation.support: Sit with the child and point to the pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the friend about one page.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Shares a picture with a friend
lessons.conclusion: Put the books in the basket and say "Thank you, books."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child choose a book each night and share it with you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose a favourite book and share it with a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 book check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child handles a book and names pictures.
successCriteria: Holds a book the right way up
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join in rhymes, name animals and greet others, and many point to pictures.
lessons.starter: Sing the book song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: book corner, picture cards and big book.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "Can you turn the page?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child names the picture and turns a page.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: book corner, picture cards and big book. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "Can you turn the page?" Children: Child names the picture and turns a page.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Book stations
practical.safety: Use sturdy books and large cards. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend a story from the pictures.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: holds a book the right way up; turns pages; names three pictures.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Close the books and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Share a book every day and name the pictures together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child handles a book and names pictures" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
